answer: Each identity catalogues one ivory artifact in the haven archive, locks a 70-credit bond, and files observations, a key signature, and a gale anchor. An archive auditor recomputes coordinates and checks the anchor against the log; a copied artifact, reused key, or bad anchor burns the bond. The fee starts at 32, rising 6 per identity: the kth fake pays 32+6(k-1), the 1000th 6026, and 1000 fakes 3,029,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-catalog ring fails: rented observations share one key and gale anchor, so a duplicate burns bonds. An honest agent pays 32 once and recovers the bond after audit.
